questions.question: If you stop at a railroad crossing with more than one track, what should you do?

options.text: Wait until you can see clearly down all tracks before you go.
Stop on the first track and watch for another train.
Go through as soon as the train passes.
Go through when one track is free.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait until you can see clearly down all tracks before you go.
questions.explanation: Do not move as soon as a train passes. Wait until you have a clear view of all tracks. Another train may be coming, even if only one track is visible.

questions.question: Which statement is true about roadwork zones?

options.text: Fines for violations in work zones are the same as normal traffic violations.
You must slow down in work zones.
Slow down only if you see workers present.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must slow down in work zones.
questions.explanation: Slow down and be ready to stop for equipment in work zones. Driving carefully protects drivers, pedestrians, cyclists, and workers.

questions.question: Where should children age 12 and under sit in a vehicle with airbags?

options.text: The front seat.
The back seat.
The bed of a pickup truck.

questions.correctAnswerText: The back seat.
questions.explanation: Airbags can be dangerous for children. Anyone age 12 or under must sit in the back seat of a vehicle with airbags.

questions.question: When you hear a siren or see flashing lights from an emergency vehicle, you must:

options.text: Slow down until it passes.
Move to the right side of the road and stop.
Wave for the vehicle to pass.
Move to the right lane and keep driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the right side of the road and stop.
questions.explanation: Give the right-of-way to any emergency vehicle using lights or sirens. Move to the right side of the road and stop. If you are in an intersection, drive through it first, then stop on the right side.

questions.question: The best way to avoid losing control on wet roads is to drive faster.

options.text: True
False

questions.correctAnswerText: False
questions.explanation: On wet roads, your tires can ride on water and you may lose control. This is called hydroplaning. Slow down when driving in wet conditions to avoid it.

questions.question: What does a red arrow on a traffic light mean?

options.text: You may turn after slowing and checking for traffic.
Do not turn until the light is green.
You may turn after stopping completely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not turn until the light is green.
questions.explanation: A red arrow means stop. You must stay stopped until a green light or green arrow appears. Never turn against a red arrow.

questions.question: Where should you keep a space cushion around your vehicle?

options.text: Only behind your vehicle.
Only on the left and right sides.
Only in front of your vehicle.
On all sides of your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: On all sides of your vehicle.
questions.explanation: Keep space all around your vehicle so you have time to react to hazards. Do not drive too close to vehicles on your left and right sides.

questions.question: When may you carefully drive through an intersection with a yellow light?

options.text: When an emergency vehicle is crossing your path.
When pedestrians are crossing.
When you are turning right.
When you are already in the intersection when the light turns yellow.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you are already in the intersection when the light turns yellow.
questions.explanation: If the light turns yellow while you are already in the intersection, you may continue through carefully.

questions.question: If you want to pass a pedestrian and an oncoming vehicle is approaching, what should you do?

options.text: Slow down and let the vehicle pass before you pass the pedestrian.
Keep steady speed. The oncoming vehicle must stop for you.
Honk to make the pedestrian move over.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and let the vehicle pass before you pass the pedestrian.
questions.explanation: Handle one hazard at a time. If you need to pass a pedestrian but a vehicle is coming, slow down and let the vehicle pass first. Then pass the pedestrian if it is safe.

questions.question: If you are driving in another driver's blind spot, what should you do?

options.text: Move ahead or fall back so the driver can see you.
Keep the same speed.
Stay in the blind spot.
Honk to let them know you are there.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move ahead or fall back so the driver can see you.
questions.explanation: Do not stay in another driver's blind spot. Move forward or drop back so the other driver can see you.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: The road to the right is one-way traffic only.
There is a detour to the right due to road construction.
The road ahead makes a sharp turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road ahead makes a sharp turn.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They alert you to dangers ahead. This sign warns drivers to slow down for a sharp turn in the road.

questions.question: If you keep a valid license for one full year without getting any traffic violations, you may get a Good Point on your driving record.

options.text: True
False

questions.correctAnswerText: True
questions.explanation: If you keep a valid driver license for one full year without getting any traffic violations, you may get a Good Point on your driving record.

questions.question: If two drivers arrive at an open intersection at the same time:

options.text: The driver on the right has the right-of-way.
The driver on the left has the right-of-way.
One driver may go without stopping.
One driver should honk to show they are giving up the right-of-way.

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver on the right has the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: If you arrive at an open intersection at the same time as a vehicle on your right, you must let that vehicle go first. You may proceed when it is safe.

questions.question: When driving in fog or mist, do not use high beam headlights because:

options.text: The light reflects back into your eyes.
Oncoming vehicles might not see you.
Vehicles behind you may follow too closely.

questions.correctAnswerText: The light reflects back into your eyes.
questions.explanation: In fog or mist, do not use high beam headlights because the light bounces back and shines in your eyes.

questions.question: Which of the following does NOT help with safe night driving?

options.text: Keep your windshield clean.
Know that tinted windows make it harder to see in the dark.
Carry a flashlight in your vehicle.
Look directly at the headlights of oncoming vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look directly at the headlights of oncoming vehicles.
questions.explanation: If you look directly at oncoming headlights, your eyes will contract. After the vehicle passes, your eyes need time to adjust back to the dark. During this time, you cannot see well and it is like driving blind.

questions.question: You may pass another vehicle if the line between your lane and the lane you want to enter is a ____ line.

options.text: Broken white
Double solid yellow
Solid yellow
Solid white

questions.correctAnswerText: Broken white
questions.explanation: White lines separate traffic moving in the same direction. You may cross broken white lines to pass when the lane is clear.

questions.question: When you see a flashing yellow light, you should:

options.text: Speed up.
Stop completely.
Turn on your headlights.
Slow down and go carefully.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and go carefully.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light warns of a hazard. Slow down and proceed carefully.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Do not enter.
Roundabout ahead.
No U-turns allowed.

questions.correctAnswerText: No U-turns allowed.
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs show traffic laws you must follow. This sign means you cannot make a U-turn.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: There is a steep hill ahead.
No trucks are allowed on the upcoming hill.
A logging road is ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: There is a steep hill ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. This sign warns drivers about a steep hill ahead. Slow down and be ready to control your speed and protect your brakes.

questions.question: Hydroplaning happens when tires slide on water instead of gripping the road. To prevent it in rain, you should:

options.text: Use cruise control to keep the same speed.
Slow down.
Move to the shoulder as soon as it rains.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: In rain, slow down to reduce hydroplaning risk. Driving too fast can make your tires lose grip on the road, making your vehicle hard to control.

questions.question: When must you yield for emergency vehicles?

options.text: Never.
When you see flashing red or blue lights or hear a siren.
Only when other vehicles yield.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you see flashing red or blue lights or hear a siren.
questions.explanation: You must give the right-of-way to any emergency vehicle using its siren or flashing lights.

questions.question: A driver entering interstate traffic from an entrance ramp should:

options.text: Yield to drivers already on the interstate.
Have the right-of-way.
Force their way into traffic.
Assume other drivers will move to make room.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to drivers already on the interstate.
questions.explanation: When entering the interstate from an acceleration ramp, yield to drivers already on the highway. Merge safely when you have space.

questions.question: What helps prevent crashes?

options.text: Communicate with other road users.
Ignore other drivers on the road.
Drive only on side streets and back roads.
Avoid driving during rush hour.

questions.correctAnswerText: Communicate with other road users.
questions.explanation: Crashes happen when drivers do unexpected things. Signal when you slow down, stop, or change direction. Use your horn or emergency signals when needed to let other drivers, bicyclists, and pedestrians know what you are doing.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Steep grade ahead.
Pedestrian crossing ahead.
Low ground railroad crossing.
Low clearance.

questions.correctAnswerText: Low clearance.
questions.explanation: This sign warns of a low overpass ahead. Do not proceed if your vehicle is taller than the height shown on the sign (13 feet 6 inches in this case).

questions.question: At a light rail intersection, you should always:

options.text: Look both ways before crossing tracks.
Pay attention and obey all traffic signals.
Share the road with pedestrians and bicyclists.
All of these.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of these.
questions.explanation: Never drive around lowered crossing gates. Always look both ways before crossing train tracks and obey all signs and signals. Trains share the road with cars and bicyclists.
